Title: Sacked Ukraine defence minister urges path to elections
Article:
KYIV: Ukraine's popular ex-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sacked last month, on Tuesday called for a move towards elections that have been put off because of the Russian invasion.
Ukraine imposed martial law when Russian forces swept over the border in February 2022, and military rule prohibits holding elections.
"Democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia," Fedorov said in a video posted to YouTube.
"We are fighting precisely because we want to remain a free European state."
Fedorov said Ukraine must find a "legal, safe, and realistic mechanism that will allow Ukraine to restore a full democratic process even amidst a prolonged war."
The ex-defence minister acknowledged the obstacles to holding a vote during the war, including how to ensure soldiers, people living near the front line and millions of Ukrainians abroad can cast ballots.
"This is complex... But complexity does not mean impossibility," Fedorov added.
Appointed defence minister in January, Fedorov tried to reform a military hit by scandals over corruption, equipment shortages, absenteeism, the treatment of conscripts and an unpopular mobilisation drive.
His dismissal in July triggered weeks of protests, piling pressure on President Volodymyr Zelenskyy who then replaced army chief Oleksandr Syrsky, widely seen as Fedorov's rival.
He gave no indication of his political plans in the video, though Fedorov has repeatedly stated that he would only return to the government as defence minister.
Zelenskyy has since appointed Yevgeniy Khmara, a career intelligence official with a low political profile, as acting defence minister pending a vote in parliament.
Another demonstration in support of Fedorov is scheduled outside parliament on Wednesday morning, according to his former adviser and key backer Sergiy Sternenko.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Palestinian-American hoists US flag on home besieged by settlers
Article:
QUSRA: A Palestinian-American has raised the US flag on his home besieged by Israeli settlers, as the United States renewed criticism of the siege that has generated condemnation around the world.
Louai Abu Ridi, who owns one of three houses in Qusra, near Nablus in the occupied West Bank, flew back from his adopted home of Ohio on Monday after settlers trapped residents inside and refused to let in food or other supplies for more than a week.
He was flying the Stars and Stripes outside his home on Tuesday and said he has asked the US embassy to keep raising his case.
"It's my message to all Americans in the United States to see what's going on here in the West Bank, how the settlers put us under siege trying to take my own house in the West Bank," Abu Ridi told AFP reporters inside his home.
Under US pressure, the Israeli military said last week it had given orders to remove the settlers.
Troops took down their tent and detained one Israeli but settlers repeatedly came back by foot or in vehicles.
"The settlers come in freely into my house and they're not doing anything," he said of the soldiers.
"They even shake hands with the settlers. It's like they're friends."
[[nid:1514362]]
Israeli settlers in the West Bank have been increasingly harassing and assaulting Palestinian residents in recent months, often with an aim to take their property.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government has pushed to support settlements backed by the Jewish right ahead of close-fought Oct 27 elections.
US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, an evangelical pastor who has long supported settlers, has offered rare criticism over the Qusra siege and said he had asked Israel to intervene.
In interviews aired late Tuesday on Israeli television, Huckabee said the United States was committed to defending its own citizens.
"We would like to see severe consequences for people who engage in – and I'll use the term – terrorist activity," Huckabee told Channel 13.
"It's not fair to the families who are Palestinian, who own their homes, who have a right to raise their families without fear," said Huckabee, who before becoming ambassador had rejected the term Palestinian.
Of the extremist settlers, Huckabee said, "If this little minority, if they think they're doing their cause a favour, they are making a horrific mistake."
Around 500,000 Israelis live in the West Bank on settlements considered illegal under international law, amid three million Palestinians.
Israel has occupied the West Bank since the 1967 Six-Day War.

Title: Govt must consider cost of living in minimum wage review, says UNI-MLC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's ongoing review of the Minimum Wages Order 2024 must consider the rising cost of living to ensure workers' incomes remain sufficient to support a decent standard of living.
UNI Malaysian Labour Centre (UNI-MLC) president Datuk Mohamed Shafie BP Mammal said fluctuations in the cost of food, housing, transportation, and education directly affected workers' purchasing power, particularly for lower-income groups.
He said the government's ongoing review of the Minimum Wages Order 2024 was important to determine whether the current rate remained relevant to workers' needs and prevailing economic conditions.
"For workers, the issue of wages is not merely about a figure on a payslip.
"The more important question is what they can afford with that wage and whether it is sufficient for them to meet their families' basic needs.
"When the cost of living changes, the real value of workers' income also changes. Therefore, wage rates need to be reviewed from time to time to ensure workers' welfare and purchasing power remain protected," he said in a statement today.
Yesterday, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan had said the government is
reviewing the RM1,700 monthly minimum wage
.
Ramanan, speaking to Utusan Malaysia, said the review takes into account key indicators, including the Poverty Line Income, median wage, Consumer Price Index, labour productivity, and unemployment rates to assess basic needs and employers' capacity to pay.
Shafie said workers were among the key pillars contributing to the country's economic growth and development, and their welfare should therefore remain a priority in labour market policy.
He said workers should not be in a situation where most of their monthly income was only enough to cover necessities, leaving little room to deal with emergencies, finance their children's education or build savings.
"Workers go to work every day to build a better life for their families. They should not only be able to pay bills and buy food, but also have some financial room to save, maintain their health, fund their children's education and deal with unexpected circumstances.
"That is the true meaning of workers' welfare. We are not talking about luxury, but about being able to live a decent life through the fruits of their own labour," he said.
However, Shafie said that the review process did not mean the minimum wage should automatically be increased.
Instead, he said, it provided an opportunity for the government, workers' representatives and employers to assess various indicators before determining whether the existing rate remained appropriate.
He said UNI-MLC was ready to provide its views and cooperation in the review process to ensure the country's wage policy remained responsive to economic changes and the realities faced by workers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two parole inmates among trio jailed 8 months for trespass
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Two inmates under the Parole Release Programme were among three men sentenced to eight months in jail for trespassing into a house last week.
Magistrate Aini Adilah Muhammad Faizal handed down the sentence to Zainudin Chik Ani, 46, Azizan Osman, 46, and Mohammad Asyraaf Zuhairi Adam Rizalee, 33, after they pleaded guilty.
Zainudin and Azizan are serving sentences under the programme and were due for full release on Sept 11.
The trio admitted to jointly committing criminal trespass by entering a 28-year-old woman's house in Jalan Padang Menora, Lahar Yooi, Tasek Gelugor, at 7.50am on Aug 12.
They were charged under Section 448 of the Penal Code, read with Section 34, which carries a maximum three-year jail term, a fine of up to RM5,000, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Lim Zhan Yi urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence.
National Legal Aid Foundation lawyer Nor Syamimi Abu Bakar, representing the trio, appealed for leniency, citing their family responsibilities.
She said Zainudin, a labourer earning RM70 a day, had a wife and child to support.
"Azizan works as a labourer earning RM60 a day. He is single but supports his mother, who suffers from heart disease.
"Mohammad Asyraaf supports his two siblings and mother while working odd jobs for RM60 a day," she told the court.
The court ordered the three men to serve their sentences from the date of their arrest.
In a separate proceeding, Zainudin was sentenced to another 10 months in jail after pleading guilty to breaking into the same house and stealing an Oppo CPH 2483 mobile phone and a set of keys, including a motorcycle key.
He was charged under Section 457 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum five-year jail term and a fine upon conviction.

Title: Temasek-backed Shiprocket jumps 35pct in debut trade after US$170mil India IPO
Article:

Its shares listed at 131 rupees on the National Stock Exchange of India, compared with an issue price of 97 rupees per share.

Title: Make it rain: Indonesia chases clouds to stem El Nino fires
Article:
INDONESIA'S Borneo, home to pristine rainforest and protected species, is burning. Meteorologist Safillah Anggie Wahyuni hopes a solution lies in the clouds.
Indonesia believes cloud seeding can help it tackle a wildfire season that experts say is on track to be among the worst in years, driven by a strong El Nino.
Indonesia's government says over 100,000 hectares burned in the first half of the year.
Independent analysis by deforestation monitoring site Nusantara Atlas puts the figure through July at over 285,000 hectares – more than four times the size of Jakarta.
Cloud seeding, which involves sprinkling silver iodide, salts or other particles into clouds to trigger precipitation, is rarely used to tackle wildfires globally.
But Indonesia is ramping up efforts, scarred by 2015 fires during a previous strong El Nino that burned through millions of hectares and created a regional haze crisis.
"Weather modification does not create clouds: we optimise clouds that have the potential to produce rains," Safillah told AFP after flying over Palangkaraya in Borneo's Central Kalimantan.
"Weather modification will only be effective if the conditions are right," she added.
Indonesia carried out 252 cloud-seeding operations between 2021 and August this year – up from 85 in the preceding decade, according to the BMKG weather agency.
Most tried to draw rain away from flooded areas, but many sought to douse wildfires or wet flammable peatlands.
In just three years since her first cloud-seeding operation, 25-year-old Safillah has accumulated more than 300 flight hours.
The technique was first used in Indonesia in 1977 to top up a dam, and the government has said dozens of helicopters and fixed-wing planes are on standby for cloud seeding nationwide.
"We are on alert to changes in weather, even the slightest, which could result in rain clouds," Security Minister Djamari Chaniago said.
But the bulk of the country's firefighting is still done on the ground, with nearly 50,000 firefighters currently deployed.
And experts question the technique's use during the dry season, when wildfires peak.
"Its effectiveness will be very low because of the lack of clouds," said I Putu Santikayasa, a hydroclimatology lecturer at IPB University south of the capital Jakarta.
Research suggests the efficacy of cloud seeding is hard to assess.
It has also raised questions about harms linked to widespread use of silver iodide, as well as the cost.
Cloud seeding is "a mitigation effort, not a permanent solution," acknowledged BMKG weather modification director Budi Harsoyo, insisting there is no evidence of harms.
[[nid:1514336]]
Research he authored found a 12-day cloud-seeding operation in 2023 doubled likely rainfall and eliminated fire hotspots.
Activists say mitigation efforts like cloud seeding ignore underlying problems, including mass conversion of rainforest and peatland.
Indonesia has large swathes of tropical peatlands.
They are an important carbon store when wet, but become highly flammable when dry and fires can smoulder underground and reignite quickly.
These vulnerable ecosystems should be protected against development, said Uli Arta Siagian, campaign coordinator with local environmental group WALHI.
"The responsibility for protection lies with the state by not issuing permits in areas that are vulnerable to fire," she told AFP.
Indonesia regularly battles devastating fires that send a choking haze over neighbours Malaysia and Singapore.
In recent days, haze from the fires has spiked air pollution levels in the Malaysian part of Borneo island, prompting several school closures.
In addition to cloud seeding, Indonesia is carrying out peatland rewetting and monitoring fire hotspots with satellites and ground patrols.
Large-scale plantations are banned from using fire to clear land, though smallholders are exempt.
But the practice remains common and is blamed for starting most of Indonesia's wildfires.
The environment minister has told local governments in vulnerable regions to beef up preventive patrols and encouraged "legal sanctions" including fines and "criminal penalties" for illegal burning.
This year's fires will be turbocharged by a powerful El Nino – a naturally occurring climate phenomenon that brings worldwide changes in winds, air pressure and rainfall patterns.
It typically causes drier conditions in Indonesia and is associated with severe fires.
The area of land burned in just the first half of this year already exceeds the area lost in all of 2023, when El Nino last formed.
Activist group 350.org warned this week that climate change is exacerbating the trend.
El Nino "arrived on top of higher global baseline temperatures, triggering more extreme weather."
* The article is from AFP

Title: [UPDATED] Family was in designated safe zone when hit by Immigration truck
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The family of four struck by an Immigration Department truck in a fatal accident at the Jalan Sultan Ismail traffic light intersection early today had been standing in a safe area when they were hit.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said investigations and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage showed that the family was in a designated pedestrian safe zone when the crash occurred.
"Based on our investigation and observations of the CCTV footage of the incident, the family was in a safe area to cross the road when they were struck by the Immigration Department truck.
"Everyone is aware that the CCTV system in the area is of a high standard and is capable of assisting us in carrying out a proper investigation.
"The drivers of the Immigration Department truck and car involved will be remanded for further investigation and action," he told reporters here today.
CCTV footage showed the family of four standing at the road divider at the Jalan Sultan Ismail traffic light intersection, opposite Maju Junction, at 1am.
At the same time, the Immigration Department truck, which was travelling from the direction of Wisma FGV along Jalan Sultan Ismail with its beacon lights switched on, entered Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman while the traffic lights were still red.
The truck was then struck by a Proton Saga travelling from the direction of Chow Kit towards Maju Junction.
Following the collision, the truck
struck the family
, leaving three of them critically injured. They were pronounced dead at the scene.
The Immigration Department truck had been on its way to Chow Kit to pick up detainees following an enforcement operation when the accident occurred.
It was earlier reported that three family members, including a 12-year-old girl, were killed after an Immigration Department truck allegedly ran a red light, struck a car, and ploughed into pedestrians along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today.
The victims, a 53-year-old man and his two daughters aged 25 and 12, died at the scene following the 1am crash at the Maju Junction traffic light intersection.
The Immigration truck, which was not carrying any detainees at the time, was driven by a 43-year-old man who was travelling from the Kuala Lumpur Immigration office to Chow Kit to pick up detainees following an operation against undocumented immigrants.
The truck is believed to have entered the intersection while the traffic light in its direction was red, with its beacon lights and siren activated.
At the same time, a Proton Saga driven by a 50-year-old man entered the intersection while the traffic light in his direction was green.
The Proton Saga driver was believed to have been unable to avoid the Immigration truck, resulting in a collision in the middle of the intersection.
The impact caused the truck to lose control and veer off before hitting four pedestrians from the same family as well as an Inokom Matrix driven by a 38-year-old man which had stopped at the intersection.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: EP Manufacturing unveils RM9.5mil chassis component plant in Tanjung Malim
Article:
IPOH: EP Manufacturing Bhd (EPMB) has unveiled a new chassis component facility in the Automotive High Technology Valley (AHTV) in Tanjong Malim, with an investment of RM9.5 million.
The facility, operated by its joint venture Peps Sanly JV Sdn Bhd (Peps Sanly JV) with China-based automotive component maker Sanly Auto Parts Co Ltd (Sanly China), will produce critical components for selected Proton Holdings Bhd (Proton) models.
The new facility marks another milestone in its nearly four-decade partnership with Proton, the company said in a statement.
The plant was officially opened yesterday by Perak Tourism, Industry, Investment and Corridor Development Committee chairman Loh Sze Yee.
Also present were EPMB executive chairman Hamidon Abdullah and Sanly China and Peps Sanly JV vice-president and director Ji Xiantao.
Hamidon said the facility marked the continuation of EPMB's strategic partnership with Sanly China, following the joint venture's formal establishment in February 2025.
"This partnership aims to build a stronger and more efficient supply chain for EPMB by leveraging Sanly China's advanced expertise in metal fabrication, assembly and automotive chassis systems.
"It is also aligned with the strategic initiatives of the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) and the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) to promote technology transfer and strengthen local manufacturing capabilities.
"More importantly, through this joint venture, EPMB and Sanly are now the only joint venture company in Malaysia focused on automotive chassis systems," he said.
Hamidon said the partnership with Sanly, which has strong ties with Geely and other Chinese original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), gives EPMB direct exposure to China's advanced manufacturing ecosystem and competitive cost structures.
This puts EPMB in a stronger position to support Proton through greater cost efficiency and enhanced quality assurance, he said.
"It also marks another step forward in our nearly four-decade partnership with Proton. We are proud to work with Proton to achieve its regional growth ambitions and electric vehicle (EV) roadmap, and we look forward to continued success together in the future," he said.
The Peps Sanly JV facility occupies 9,909 square metres and began operations in October 2025. It has the capacity to produce 40,000 vehicle sets a month, or up to 480,000 sets annually.
The facility will undertake local production of front-corner modules, subframe modules and rear-axle modules for Proton's AMA01, Persona and Iriz models, as well as the upcoming AMA02 and AMA05 models.
In February 2025, EPMB announced the formal establishment of its joint venture with Sanly China through Peps Sanly JV to undertake local production of front-corner, subframe and rear-axle modules for the Proton Saga AMA01.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration truck crash: Family were on KL holiday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The three family members killed in a crash involving an Immigration Department truck along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today are believed to have been in the capital for a holiday.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said police had yet to establish when the family arrived in the capital, how long they planned to stay or where they were staying.
"We have yet to verify the finer details of when they came to KL and how long and where they were staying here.
"The surviving family member is currently receiving medical treatment at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL), and we want to give her some time and let the situation calm down before we take her statement," he said when contacted today.
It was reported that three family members, including a 12-year-old girl, were killed after an Immigration Department truck allegedly
ran a red light
, struck a car, and ploughed into pedestrians along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today.
The victims, a 53-year-old man and his daughters, aged 25 and 12, died at the scene following the 1am crash at the Maju Junction traffic light intersection.
The Immigration truck, driven by a 43-year-old man, was travelling from the Kuala Lumpur Immigration office to Chow Kit to pick up detainees following an operation against undocumented migrants.
The truck was not carrying any detainees at the time.
The truck is believed to have entered the intersection while the traffic light in its direction was red, with its beacon lights and siren activated.
At the same time, a Proton Saga driven by a 50-year-old man entered the intersection while the traffic light in his direction was green.
The Proton Saga driver was believed to have been unable to avoid the Immigration truck, resulting in a collision in the middle of the intersection.
The impact sent the truck veering off course before it struck the four pedestrians from the same family and an Inokom Matrix driven by a 38-year-old man, which had stopped at the intersection.

Title: Child sex assault at Singapore mosque triggers review of safeguards
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore's acting Minister-in-Charge of Muslim Affairs has ordered a review of mosque safeguards after an unaccredited religious influencer was jailed for sexually abusing five victims, including two young brothers.
Zaqy Mohamad said the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) was directed to examine safety protocols at mosques after one of the offences occurred inside a mosque toilet.
He described the case as deeply troubling, given that several offences took place at a mosque where religious guidance and community interactions occurred.
Zaqy added that MUIS is working with relevant organisations to ensure the victims' family receives necessary care and support.
The 37-year-old self-proclaimed religious influencer was sentenced on Aug 17 to 27 years and 10 months' imprisonment and 24 strokes of the cane.
The court heard that the man assumed a father-figure role in the lives of two young brothers whose parents were absent.
He repeatedly raped the younger brother, aged between six and eight at the time, at various locations, including a mosque toilet.
He also molested the elder brother, then aged 11 to 12, on multiple occasions.
Additionally, the man molested three other victims, including a 17-year-old boy who regarded him as a mentor.
Zaqy is currently serving as acting minister-in-charge following the resignation of former minister Faishal Ibrahim.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor Amanah sets up committee to monitor Rohingya issues
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor Amanah will set up a special committee to monitor issues involving the Rohingya refugee community amid concerns over public order, law compliance and tensions with local residents.
Johor Amanah chairman Aminolhuda Hassan said the committee would gather complaints and information from residents before referring matters requiring action to the relevant authorities.
"We do not want these issues to go unchecked until they create tension between the community and local residents," he said in a statement today.
Aminolhuda said the committee would also urge the state and federal governments to strengthen the management of refugee settlements, documentation, economic activities and compliance with the law.
He said that any offence should be dealt with according to the law, regardless of a person's status or background.
The move follows growing concerns among residents over the presence and activities of refugee communities, particularly those involving public order and enforcement.
Aminolhuda said the committee would provide Johoreans with a responsible channel to submit complaints, information and suggestions, rather than allowing unverified claims to spread on social media and fuel hostility.
He also called for a more structured mechanism for the placement and monitoring of refugees involving security agencies, local authorities and the Federal Government.
"This is about ensuring the safety, peace and wellbeing of Johoreans while ensuring refugee management is carried out firmly, systematically and humanely," he said.

Title: [UPDATED] Immigration Dept to conduct internal probe into fatal Jalan Sultan Ismail crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department will conduct an internal investigation into compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) and safety measures following a fatal accident involving one of its vehicles along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the review would focus on procedures and safety aspects governing departmental vehicles.
He said the department viewed the incident seriously and would take appropriate action based on the findings of the police investigation and its internal probe.
The department confirmed that one of its vehicles was involved in the accident in the early hours of Aug 19.
Zakaria expressed condolences to the victims' families and said the department was praying for those injured to recover.
"The Immigration Department is giving its cooperation to police in their investigation to determine the cause and actual circumstances of the incident.
"The department respects the ongoing investigation and will not make any conclusions that could pre-empt the findings of the authorities," he said.
He also urged anyone with information on the crash to assist police.
Zakaria called on the public to respect the privacy and sensitivities of the victims' families and refrain from circulating unverified photographs, recordings or information that could fuel speculation or affect the investigation.
It was reported that three members of a family, including a 12-year-old girl, were
killed after an Immigration truck allegedly ran a red light,
crashed into a car and ploughed into pedestrians at the Maju Junction traffic light intersection around 1am.
The victims, a 53-year-old man and his daughters, aged 25 and 12, died at the scene.
The Immigration truck, which was not carrying detainees at the time, was driven by a 43-year-old man travelling from the Kuala Lumpur Immigration office to Chow Kit to pick up detainees following an operation against undocumented immigrants.
The truck is believed to have entered the intersection while the traffic light was red, with its beacon lights and siren activated.
At the same time, a Proton Saga driven by a 50-year-old man entered the intersection when the light was green.
The Saga driver was believed to have been unable to avoid the Immigration truck, resulting in a collision.
The impact caused the truck to lose control and veer off before hitting four pedestrians from the same family and an Inokom Matrix driven by a 38-year-old man, which had stopped at the intersection.
The victims' 55-year-old mother suffered injuries to her head, right hand and both legs and was taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for treatment.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: KL police destroy RM15.4m worth of drugs seized since 2007
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur police are disposing of more than RM15.4 million worth of drugs seized in cases dating back to 2007, following the completion of court proceedings.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the disposal involved 5,022 drug exhibits from 4,884 investigation papers opened between 2007 and 2025.
He said all the cases had resulted in convictions.
"The disposal involves 544.28kg of drugs in solid form and 963.34 litres in liquid form, with a total estimated street value of RM15,448,631.65.
"The drugs could have been abused by 382,739 users," he said at a drug exhibit disposal event here today.
Among the drugs being destroyed are 65.21kg of MDMA, 54.39kg of methamphetamine, 33.10kg of ketamine, 7.98kg of nimetazepam, 6.60kg of heroin and 124.73g of cocaine.
Police are also disposing of 17.65kg of cannabis, 359.21kg of ketum leaves, 960.39 litres of ketum liquid and 2.95 litres of codeine.
Fadil said the exhibits were linked to convictions under Sections 39B, 39A(2), 39A(1), 6 and 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, as well as Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952.
He said the exhibits would be destroyed in collaboration with Kualiti Alam Sdn Bhd at its scheduled waste-to-energy incineration facility at the Bukit Pelandok Waste Management Centre in Negri Sembilan.
He said the exercise was important not only to destroy the drugs but also to safeguard the integrity of evidence and prevent seized drugs from re-entering circulation.
"We want to avoid any perception or misunderstanding among the public about what happens to the tonnes or hundreds of kilogrammes of drugs seized by police.
"There is a set process, beginning with arrest and seizure, followed by investigation, prosecution, conviction and, finally, disposal," he added.
Fadil said drug exhibits could only be destroyed after all necessary legal processes had been completed, with some cases taking considerable time to conclude.
Clearing old exhibits would also ease the burden on personnel responsible for safeguarding them and address storage constraints, he said.
"Many of these exhibits can also have negative effects on the environment. When they are kept in evidence storage facilities, personnel guarding them can sometimes be exposed to such risks," he added.

Title: Singapore: No construction waste exported for disposal in Johor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Singapore does not allow construction and demolition (C&D) waste to be exported for disposal, its National Environment Agency (NEA) says following reports of such waste being dumped illegally in Pontian, Johor.
NEA said it had contacted the Johor Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) to seek more information on C&D waste reportedly originating from Singapore.
"During the call with SWCorp, NEA affirmed that Singapore does not allow C&D waste to be exported for disposal," it said in response to queries from The Straits Times on Aug 18.
NEA said nine companies identified by SWCorp as being linked to the illegal dumping were Malaysian companies.
It said it had yet to establish whether any Singapore companies were involved, adding that C&D waste must be processed and sorted in Singapore.
Previously, the New Straits Times reported that Kepong member of parliament Lim Lip Eng had called on authorities to explain how construction waste allegedly brought in from Singapore entered Pontian, amid claims by residents that about 20 trailers make the journey almost every night.
Lim said residents
claimed the waste had been transported
into the district for about two years now , raising questions over cargo inspections and border controls.
NEA said it had also issued an advisory to licensed general waste disposal facilities handling C&D waste in Singapore, reminding them of the relevant requirements.
Under Singapore's regulatory framework, C&D waste must be properly processed and sorted locally for recycling.
However, homogeneous material streams recovered from such waste, including ferrous scrap, are considered recyclables and may be exported, subject to relevant regulatory requirements.
NEA said it took a serious view of illegal waste disposal, which could pollute the environment and pose a public health hazard, and would continue working with Malaysian authorities to investigate the matter.
Johor SWCorp has opened four investigation papers into possible offences involving the disposal, storage and transfer of controlled solid waste.
Residents in Pontian had previously reported convoys of lorries travelling at night to several sites to dump construction debris, including cement, broken tiles and used construction equipment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia still exposed to oil price swings despite LNG strength – Kenanga Research
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The recent oil shock has exposed a less visible vulnerability in Malaysia's energy balance, even as the country remains a net energy exporter, said Kenanga Research.
However, Malaysia's fiscal position remains exposed to refined product prices through subsidies, while its trade position shows a crude oil deficit but a liquefied natural gas (LNG) surplus.
"Malaysia is a net oil importer, but LNG is what makes Malaysia's energy balance positive. In 2025, Malaysia ran a RM30.4 billion deficit in crude and condensate and only a RM3.2 billion surplus in refined products, resulting in a combined petroleum deficit of RM27.2 billion.
"The overall oil and gas surplus of RM18.2 billion exists because of a RM45.4 billion LNG surplus," the bank said in a research note today.
Kenanga said fuel subsidies are linked to refined product prices, while LNG receipts accrue to a different fiscal line and arrive with a lag.
"Higher oil prices therefore protect the budget far less than the overall energy export position implies," it said.
According to estimates by the Finance Ministry, every US$1 per barrel (bbl) increase in oil prices raises federal petroleum revenue by RM300 million annually, excluding dividends from Petronas.
However, the bank estimates an annual increase of around RM1.05 billion for each US$1/bbl move.
Kenanga noted that the fiscal exposure is further compounded by relatively low subsidy "strike" levels.
"The fiscal exposure has a relatively low strike. We put the RON95 subsidy strike at around US$44/bbl Brent and the diesel strike at around US$48/bbl following the RM2.10 BUDI Diesel price, both on a futures basis.
"Neither strike is close to our US$80/bbl average house-view for 2026, so the exposure persists even without another major oil shock," it explained.
The bank pointed out that the targeted subsidy measures have helped to reduce the fiscal burden.
BUDI95 is delivering estimated annual savings of RM2.5 billion to RM4.0 billion, and BUDI Diesel a further RM2.0 billion from July.
Combined, these targeted subsidy initiatives could save RM4.5 billion to RM6.0 billion annually.
It added that the Finance Ministry has consistently framed the savings as fiscal space for education, healthcare and public transport infrastructure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: F1 Malaysia return marred by ticket scalping, booking woes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The return of Formula One to Malaysia has sparked excitement and frustration among fans, with complaints of ticket scalping, long virtual queues and problems with official ticketing platforms.
The biggest concern centres on the RM200 Madani G Hillstand ticket, a subsidised category available exclusively to Malaysian MyKad holders.
Fans on social media alleged that scalpers bought the tickets in bulk and resold them for up to RM400 to RM600 — as much as three times the original price.
Threads user fiq66 said scalpers were reselling the RM200 tickets for RM400 to RM600, describing it as "easy money".
Other users reported being quoted RM350 and RM500, while some urged fans to avoid resellers offering Madani tickets for RM600.
International fans also reported paying hefty markups after struggling to secure tickets through official channels.
A Reddit user on r/GrandPrixTravel said their family eventually bought tickets through a reseller at three times the normal price, while questioning the lack of advance notification on official F1 social media accounts and email newsletters.
The Madani ticket is the cheapest of six three-day ticket categories for Malaysians, with prices ranging from RM200 for the G Hillstand to RM2,083.40 for the Main Grandstand.
Other categories include the K1 Grandstand at RM1,386, F Grandstand at RM1,291.40, and B and C Hillstands at RM809.60.
International fans are charged in US dollars, with the Main Grandstand priced at US$566.05.
Fans also complained about long virtual queues and difficulties accessing ticketing websites.
User iForgotMyOldAcc on Reddit highlighted that the booking systems appeared particularly vulnerable to scalping.
"Selling this much in two to three days is still impressive, though I notice their booking system is really vulnerable to scalping, so there's probably a lot of that going on," they wrote.
Beyond scalping, fans encountered significant difficulty purchasing through official channels.
Multiple users, both local and international, on Reddit's r/GrandPrixTravel and r/Bolehland forums reported that the Bahrain International Circuit website was either non-functional or extremely slow, with one Reddit user claiming that the site "doesn't accept Malaysian cards."
One user said they tried five internationally used credit cards on the BahrainGP website without success and ultimately purchased through a third-party seller at a €100 markup.
Users claimed official ticketing websites did not fare well under the surge of demand, forcing fans to look towards official third-party resellers and reseller marketplaces.
One Reddit user reported purchasing through a third-party company after being 55,000 places deep in the queue on the F1 platform.
Another user said they were 38,000 deep in the queue before similarly pivoting, highlighting that they never received any of the pre-sale email notifications they had signed up for.
The race, scheduled for Oct 2 to 4 at the Sepang International Circuit, marks Formula One's return to Malaysia for the first time since 2017.
The event is being held as a replacement for the Bahrain Grand Prix, which could not take place as originally scheduled.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump pauses 50pct tariffs on Canadian goods for three days
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump paused the planned rollout of new tariffs on Canadian goods late Tuesday, after negotiations between both countries that went down to the wire.
The temporary reprieve from the 50-per cent duties would last three days, the US leader said in a social media post. The tariffs were originally set to take effect Wednesday.
The delay was "based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalization of documents, have a DEAL!" Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.
Trump's announcement came after he held urgent talks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Tuesday afternoon, hours before the duties were due to come into place.
The leaders also spoke Monday, after Carney told reporters that discussions to avert the duties were at an "intense and delicate" stage.
The US Trade Representative's office said on X that the pact between Washington and Ottawa is set to "include comprehensive market access for all American goods, economic security commitments, digital trade alignment" and other provisions.
A proclamation by Trump to pause the duties added that the suspension came about as "Canada has expressed a commitment to remove the discriminations or unreasonable and unequal impositions at issue."
DISCRIMINATORY TREATMENT
Trump had signed orders for the steep 50-per cent duties last month, with the White House alleging "discriminatory treatment" by Canada against US alcohol, automobile and dairy products.
The tariffs cover products such as wine, hockey sticks and cement.
Trump's planned tariffs target around 5.5 per cent of Canada's exports to the United States, worth about US$20 billion, Oxford Economics estimates.
While this only poses a "modest" negative risk to Canada's economy, Oxford Economics said in a recent report that the duties would "affect central Canada's manufacturing sector much more severely."
Canadian negotiators have been in Washington to push for a deal to avoid the new tariffs and also secure relief on Trump's sector-specific duties -- which have battered Canada's auto, steel, lumber and aluminum industries.
Ottawa reportedly offered concessions like pressuring provinces to put US alcohol and wine back on their shelves, Canadian media said.
Without going into details, Trump added in his Truth Social post: "The great Keystone XL Pipeline, long ago killed by Sleepy Joe Biden, may be awoken from the grave!"
Trump has previously called for the revival of the controversial project opposed by environmental activists, which was blocked under his predecessor Joe Biden.
POLITICAL CONCERNS
"It's not unusual for a trade negotiation to go right up to the deadline," former US commerce official Christopher Padilla told AFP.
He expects that the Trump administration threatened new tariffs to try and win early concessions from Canada as the countries negotiate over renewing the US-Mexico-Canada free trade agreement (USMCA).
Oxford Economics anticipates that manufacturers who stand to be most impacted include those in the cement, paper, printing, wood, clothing and electronic equipment sectors.
With the US Supreme Court striking down many of Trump's global tariffs earlier this year, the president had tapped an untested legal provision for the new duties targeting Canada.
The US duties will not apply to Canadian energy, potash or goods already facing sector-specific tariffs, but are set to hit products covered by the USMCA.
Trump's trade envoy Jamieson Greer previously said the tariffs aimed to "hold Canada accountable" for its retaliation against the United States.
Provinces have taken US alcohol products off their shelves, he said, and "given better market access to dairy products from the European Union" among other actions, Greer said in July.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Norliza charged again, this time over RM13.4mil in unlawful proceeds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An investment company director, who was previously charged with criminal breach of trust, was brought before the Sessions Court here again today to face 10 charges of receiving RM13.4 million in proceeds from unlawful activities.
Datuk Norliza Tajudin, 54, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out individually before Judge Suzana Hussin.
She is accused of receiving the money through cheques and online transfers from an Energy Eco Bhd bank account, with the funds allegedly transferred to her personal account and an account belonging to Aura Emas Trading Sdn Bhd, of which she is a director.
The offences allegedly took place at three bank branches in Taman Setiawangsa, Wangsa Melawati and Bangsar between Feb 1, 2021 and Feb 2, 2024.
Norliza was charged under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613), punishable under Section 4(1) of the same Act.
The offence carries a maximum 15-year jail term and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the proceeds, or RM5 million, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nurul Qistini Qamarul Abrar applied for the existing RM100,000 bail and conditions imposed in Norliza's earlier CBT case to remain.
"The prosecution also applies for this case to be tried jointly with the previous case (criminal breach of trust) in this court," she said.
Lawyer Datuk Gobinath Mohanna, representing Norliza, did not object.
Suzana granted the application and ordered the two cases to be tried jointly. She fixed Oct 29 for mention.
On May 11, Norliza and former Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Syariah Advisory Council chairman Tan Sri Dr Mohd Daud Bakar
pleaded not guilty
in the same court to seven charges of CBT involving RM10.55 million.
The court granted each accused RM100,000 bail in one surety and ordered them to surrender their passports, refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses and report to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office monthly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police send special team to Islamabad over Malaysians held in scam raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have dispatched a special team to Islamabad, Pakistan, to investigate reports regarding the detention of several Malaysians suspected of involvement in an online scam syndicate.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said he could not confirm the exact number of Malaysians detained as the investigation was still in its early stages.
He said the Home Minister informed him yesterday that visits to specific locations require coordinated action, not just between police, but also on a government-to-government level.
Khalid said police were actively tracing the network of individuals involved in these activities with the cooperation of Pakistani authorities.
The developments follow reports by international media yesterday that Pakistani authorities had detained 258 foreign nationals during a
raid on a scam call centre
in the Gulberg Green residential area on the outskirts of Islamabad.
The arrests involved 40 Chinese nationals and 170 Vietnamese nationals, in addition to Malaysians and citizens from other Asian countries.
Khalid revealed that current trends show online scam activities increasingly involve foreign nationals, particularly those from China.
He noted that the National Scam Response Centre in Cyberjaya receives over 500 calls from victims daily, with every complaint followed up by a police report to enable the Commercial Crime Investigation Department to take immediate action.
He said the severity of the issue was evident with the arrest of 182 foreign nationals last month who were attempting to turn Malaysia into a hub for online scam activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] 'Red light means stop': Road safety group warns official duties are no excuse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Government vehicle drivers must not treat official duties as a licence to disregard road traffic laws, the Road Safety Expert Association (PPKJR) said following a reported incident involving an Immigration Department vehicle that allegedly ran a red light and resulted in the
deaths of 3 people
.
Its founder and road safety and motorsport advisor Jamil Manan Supri said running a red light was not a minor traffic offence and could result in sudden and fatal collisions with road users travelling lawfully.
"A red light means stop, it is not a suggestion.
"When the traffic light is red, drivers must stop. It does not matter whether the road appears empty, whether the driver is in a hurry, whether the vehicle belongs to the government or who is behind the wheel," he said in a statement today.
Jamil said excuses such as being in a hurry, believing the road was empty or carrying out official duties should not be used to normalise violations of basic road safety rules.
"A few seconds saved can cost another person their life," he said.
He said drivers of government departments and agencies, including those operating enforcement, operational and official vehicles, remained responsible for driving carefully and responsibly and complying with road traffic laws, subject to applicable legal provisions and legitimate operational circumstances.
"Government vehicles are not above the law. Government drivers are not above the law.
"Official duties should never be used as an excuse to take unnecessary risks with the lives of other road users," he said.
PPKJR said it extended its condolences to the families of the three victims and stressed that appropriate action should be taken promptly if investigations confirmed that a red-light violation and negligent driving contributed to the tragedy.
[[nid:1514354]]
Jamil also called on ministries, departments and agencies operating official vehicles to strengthen defensive and high-risk driving training, ensure strict compliance with standard operating procedures and monitor driver behaviour, particularly for high-risk offences such as running red lights, speeding and dangerous overtaking.
He also urged agencies to conduct regular driver and vehicle safety audits and consider using technology such as dashboard cameras and vehicle monitoring systems, where appropriate and in accordance with agency policies.
"We must move away from the culture of 'crash happens, investigate, take action' towards 'identify the risk, prevent it, monitor it, act before tragedy occurs'," he said.
Jamil said weaknesses in driver procedures, training or management should be addressed before another tragedy occurs.
"An official vehicle may have an important mission. But human life is far more important.
"Red means stop. The law applies to everyone. Official duties are not a licence to drive dangerously," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's 4pct-5pct growth forecast now looks conservative, says economist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's full-year growth forecast of between 4.0 and 5.0 per cent is now seen as conservative after the economy outperformed expectations in the first half of the year, an economist said.
Dr Geoffrey Williams said Malaysia had shown resilience and was not suffering from an economic downturn despite the geopolitical crisis, mainly due to government policies.
He said the government had focused on protecting consumers and businesses by keeping petrol and diesel prices low while absorbing the fiscal impact.
This has allowed consumers and businesses to carry out their day-to-day activities without worrying too much about the economic impact of the crisis.
Williams added that technology-driven areas of Malaysia's economy, such as the artificial intelligence boom, the rise of data centres and the semiconductor sector, were supporting overall economic growth, as reflected in the gross domestic product figures for the first and second quarters.
"For the next half of the year, I expect there is no reason why there will be a slowdown. We can expect this momentum to continue into the end of the year.
"The Finance Ministry's growth forecast of between 4.0 and 5.0 per cent is now looking to be conservative. We are likely to reach the upper-end of that range or above 5.0 per cent economic growth for the year as a whole," he said in his keynote address at the Logistics Symposium 2026 here today.
Malaysia's economy expanded 5.7 per cent in the first half of the year, driven by growth of 5.4 per cent in the first quarter and 6.0 per cent in the second quarter.
Robust domestic demand, as well as notable gains across the services, manufacturing and construction sectors, contributed to the economic performance.
Williams said Malaysia was now in a "much better situation" than it should be based on economic analysis.
"We should be in a period of caution and slowdown, people should be changing their plans.
"But actually we are in a situation where we are experiencing very high economic growth in the first half and very good growth is expected in the second half and the year as a whole. That is not going to go away quickly and it is growing momentum year on year," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nilai university CFO claims trial over RM6.56mil CBT
Article:
SEREMBAN: The chief financial officer (CFO) of a private university in Nilai pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of criminal breach of trust involving RM6.56 million in company funds between September last year and April this year.
Noraini Aripin, 55, entered the plea after the charge was read before Judge Datin M. Kunasundary Marimuthu.
She is accused of misusing RM6,557,720 entrusted to her by making payments for purposes other than ad valorem duty to the Inland Revenue Board (IRB).
The offence allegedly took place at the university's office between September 2025 and April 2026.
Noraini was charged under Section 409 of the Penal Code (Act 574), which carries a maximum 20-year jail term, whipping and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Syairah Aqilah Khalil proposed bail of RM100,000 with two sureties, with Noraini also required to surrender her passport and report monthly to the Negri Sembilan Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office.
However, lawyer Kelvin Ong sought a reduction to RM50,000, citing his client's status as a mother of five, her ongoing treatment for stage-three breast cancer at a private hospital and monthly income of RM15,000.
The court set bail at RM80,000 with two sureties and granted all the prosecution's other requests.
The court fixed Sept 21 for mention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chin Hin, UCSI team up on Melaka education hub
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Chin Hin Group Property Bhd (CHGP) is partnering UCSI Group to establish an integrated education hub that will anchor its 7.81-hectare waterfront masterplan within the Melaka Waterfront Economic Zone.
The partnership aims to strengthen the developer's push to create an education-led mixed-use destination.
The development will combine education, residential, lifestyle, commercial and future healthcare components, with the education hub positioned as a key catalyst for population growth, talent attraction and economic activity.
In a statement, CHGP said the purpose-built campus will house UCSI International School and Sekolah Sri UCSI, with capacity for up to 3,000 students and boarding facilities for up to 300 students.
The wider waterfront development will comprise serviced residences, retail and lifestyle offerings, educational facilities and a future healthcare component, creating an integrated ecosystem designed to serve students, families, residents, professionals and visitors.
CHGP's wholly-owned subsidiary Chin Hin PMC Sdn Bhd and UCSI will establish a joint venture (JV) company to develop and operate the school. CHGP will hold a 30 per cent strategic stake in the JV, with UCSI owning the remaining 70 per cent.
According to CHGP, the JV will acquire a designated leasehold land parcel within the development for the school campus.
UCSI will manage the school's education and operations, while CHGP will oversee the campus development.
The partnership will allow CHGP to participate in the education sector's long-term growth and recurring income potential, said the company's group chief executive officer of the property development division, Chang Tze Yoong.
"Together with UCSI, we are establishing a key catalyst for community growth, talent attraction and long-term value creation across the broader development," he said.
He said the integration of education, residential, lifestyle and future healthcare components is expected to support CHGP's longer-term growth strategy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MSC shares down 2.06pct in early trade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Smelting Corporation Bhd's (MSC) share price fell 2.06 per cent in early trading on Wednesday, following the announcement of a temporary suspension of its mining operations yesterday.
At 10.34 am, its shares slid four sen to RM1.90, with 1.41 million shares traded.
The company said the Perak Department of Minerals and Geosciences (JMG Perak) directed its 80 per cent-owned subsidiary, Rahman Hydraulic Tin Sdn Bhd (RHT), to suspend mining operations temporarily.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, MSC said the directive, effective Aug 12, 2026, follows a site inspection conducted by JMG Perak at RHT's tin mine in Klian Intan, after about 60 millimetres of rainfall was recorded within one hour on Aug 3, 2026.
In a note, Public Investment Bank Bhd said initial estimates suggest that if operations were to be halted for three weeks and quarterly production falls by 25 per cent, the mining segment could incur a pre-tax profit loss of about RM15 million to RM20 million.
This would reduce their financial year 2026 (FY2026) earnings forecast by 11-15 per cent.
"However, we keep our earnings forecast unchanged for now, pending further discussions with management.
"Despite this temporary operational setback, we remain positive on both the tin market and MSC's prospects. We maintain our "Outperform" call with an unchanged target price of RM3.10," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dollar drifts near multi-month lows as Treasury yields ease; Fed minutes awaited
Article:
HONG KONG: The US dollar drifted near multi-month lows against major peers on Wednesday as Treasury yields eased from recent highs, with investors awaiting minutes of the Federal Reserve's latest policy meeting for clues on the path of interest rates.
The euro inched higher to US$1.1577, remaining close to the two-month high touched earlier this week.
Sterling was little changed at US$1.3533, holding near a three-month high ahead of British inflation data due later on Wednesday, which is widely expected to show persistent price pressure.
The Japanese yen was little changed at 159.56 per dollar, having given back much of its intervention gains, but it is still well off a multi-decade low of about 164.
The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six major peers, was down marginally at 99.65.
A selloff in US Treasuries appeared to have paused amid a week light on economic data or other obvious catalysts. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note extended declines and was last at 4.702 per cent, while that on the 30-year bond fell to 5.282 per cent.
Market participants now turn to the Federal Reserve's release of minutes from the most recent meeting of its monetary policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee later in the day, looking for clues as to policymakers' views on interest rates.
Data released in the past few weeks have pointed to a softer US economy, including unexpected job losses in July and mild inflation readings, leading investors to scale back rate-hike bets.
"If the Fed does not follow through with the rate hikes that are being discounted, the upside for bond yields should be very limited here," Harvinder Kalirai, chief global fixed income and currency strategist at Alpine Macro, said in a client webcast.
"The labour market and inflation surprise are rolling over and usually that coincides with a narrowing in the dollar's yield advantage, and that feeds through into a softer dollar."
Meanwhile, a stalemate in the Middle East lifted oil prices to near three-week highs, keeping inflation risk alive. US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday there were no talks with Iran and insisted the Strait of Hormuz was open, contradicting Iran's assertion that the waterway remained shut to shipping.
Elsewhere, the New Zealand dollar and the Australian dollar were little changed, last trading at US$0.5874 and US$0.7083, respectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Former investment bank CEO charged with RM139.8mil fraud
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A former chief executive officer of an investment bank pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court today to cheating involving a RM139.8 million payment to a private university management company.
Razlan Raghazli, 43, the former CEO of UBB Investment Bank Limited, entered the plea after the charge was read out before judge Azura Alwi.
He was charged with deceiving UBB Amanah Bhd managing director and CEO Aida Aizura Othman, 52, into believing that a payment schedule in a UBB Investment Bank Limited letter complied with legal advice.
The letter, titled "Disbursement Advice on Islamic Property Financing Under Bai-Bithaman Ajil (BBA)" and dated Sept 18, 2025, was signed by the accused and stated that it followed legal advice from Kassim Tadin, Wai & Co.
However, the accused allegedly knew that the payment schedule contradicted the law firm's advice.
The deception allegedly induced Aida Aizura to release RM139,891,776 to ELMU Higher Education Sdn Bhd, which she would not have done had she not been misled.
The offence, under Section 420 of the Penal Code, was allegedly committed at the bank in Desa Sri Hartamas in September 2025.
He faces imprisonment of up to 10 years, whipping, and is liable to a fine upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Hazel Tan Jia Qi proposed bail of RM100,000 with one surety, along with additional conditions requiring the accused to surrender his passport to the court and prohibiting him from interfering with or communicating with prosecution witnesses in the case.
However, lawyer Azamuddin Abdul Aziz, representing Razlan, requested that the bail amount be reduced to RM50,000, citing that his client had been unemployed since last June and had to support four children as well as an ailing mother.
Azura then set bail at RM60,000 with the additional conditions requested by the prosecution.
She also set Oct 12 for mention and the submission of documents.
Meanwhile, the proceedings drew attention when lawyer Johan Mohan Abdullah, who is holding a watching brief for UBB, requested a court order prohibiting the media from naming the financial institution in their reports.
He argued that reports naming the institution could potentially undermine financial stability and trigger panic among depositors. However, Azura maintained that the public has a right to know further details regarding the case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Equal isn't fair: Bangi MP calls for voter-based funding model
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Constituency allocations for members of parliament should take into account not only equal access but also the number of voters and circumstances of each constituency, said Bangi MP Syahredzan Johan.
He said while there had been growing calls for equal allocations for all MPs, including legislation to guarantee such funding regardless of political affiliation, equality did not necessarily translate into fairness.
Syahredzan said Bangi had more than 300,000 registered voters as of 2022, a figure he believed had increased over the past few years.
He said the constituency had roughly three times the national average number of registered voters.
"Let us look at Bangi's neighbours. Hulu Langat has around 160,000 voters, Putrajaya has 42,000, and Puchong has about 150,000 voters," he said in a Facebook post.
Yesterday, DAP called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to immediately fulfil Pakatan Harapan's election pledge
to provide equal Constituency Development Fund
allocations to all MPs.
The party also called for the commitment to be enshrined in law to remove political discretion from the allocation process.
DAP chairman Gobind Singh Deo said the party had raised the matter with the prime minister on numerous occasions and urged him to take action without further delay.
Syahredzan added that Bangi had more than 700,000 residents, meaning its MP effectively had to serve a much larger population than the number of registered voters.
"The member of parliament for Bangi effectively needs to serve 700,000 people, not just 300,000, as he or she cannot discriminate or distinguish between voters and non-voters in the constituency," he said.
Syahredzan said discussions on constituency funding must therefore consider both equality of access and fairness in the amount allocated, based on parameters such as the number of voters.
He said allocations for service centres and staffing should also take geographical factors into account, as the cost of maintaining offices and staff could vary significantly between regions.
At the same time, development allocations should reflect the differing needs of rural and urban constituencies, he said.
"Rural areas require more infrastructure projects than urban ones," he said.
Syahredzan said legislation should be introduced to codify constituency funding for all MPs regardless of their political affiliation.
He said DAP would support Anwar's efforts to introduce such legislation.
However, he stressed that the legislation should ensure not only equal access to constituency allocations but also a fair and proportionate distribution based on the number of voters and the unique circumstances of each constituency.
"This is not for the MP, who will come and go, but to ensure fairness for those who are in mega constituencies such as Bangi," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TH depositors: Truth must not be hidden after RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Tabung Haji (TH) depositors have described the disclosure of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report as an important and courageous step towards restoring the institution's integrity, governance and public confidence.
Bank executive Anis Atifah Che Rawi, 39, a TH depositor since she was 25, welcomed the disclosure, saying it would allow depositors to understand the situation and ensure issues were addressed fairly and transparently.
"This report is important to understand what is really happening. As a TH depositor, I hope this issue can be addressed transparently and fairly so that public confidence in TH remains intact," she told Bernama.
She also welcomed the government's assurance that depositors' savings remained protected under the Tabung Haji Act 1995, adding that it provided peace of mind and reflected the government's commitment to safeguarding Muslims' interests.
Anis Atifah also supported continued legal action against those found to have committed misconduct and called for greater transparency in TH's management.
"If there is any misconduct, the matter needs to be investigated according to the law. What is important is that TH's management must continue to be strengthened so that depositors' confidence can be maintained," she said.
Pertubuhan Mesra Pengguna Malaysia (PMPM) deputy president Azlin Othman, 49, who has been a TH depositor for 31 years, shared the view, describing the RCI disclosure as an important turning point in improving the institution's governance.
Azlin said she was relieved that weaknesses in TH's previous governance had been openly revealed.
"I was disappointed and shocked when I read about how badly TH was managed before. But I am also relieved because finally the truth has come out and is no longer hidden," she said.
She said strict action against those suspected of misconduct was appropriate and hoped efforts to improve TH's governance would be carried out without political interference.
Meanwhile, a solid waste disposal contract worker who wished to be known as Raja Mustaffa, 40, said the RCI's disclosure had allowed the institution's problems to be identified and addressed.
The father of two said the government's guarantee under the TH Act provided assurance that depositors' savings remained safe.
"Honestly, I felt disappointed when I found out that the savings of Muslims were managed with such weaknesses.
"But I am now relieved because finally this issue has been opened transparently. At least we know the real problem and can fix it instead of covering it up," he said.
Raja Mustaffa also welcomed asset recovery and restructuring measures aimed at making TH's investment management more transparent and professional, with independent oversight to prevent similar mistakes from recurring.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Education Ministry builds 2,102 classrooms for 2027 Year One intake
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  The Education Ministry is implementing 681 projects nationwide to build 2,102 additional classrooms to accommodate increased Year One enrolment for the 2027 academic session.
The ministry said RM668 million had been allocated for 524 projects in Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan, involving 1,780 classrooms — 1,255 mainstream and 525 Integrated Special Education Programme (PPKI) classrooms.
The projects will accommodate an additional 43,925 mainstream pupils and 5,250 PPKI pupils.
In Sarawak, 84 projects costing RM81.5 million are underway to build 210 classrooms, while 73 projects costing RM58 million are being implemented in Sabah to build 112 classrooms.
Several projects, including at SK Durian Mas, SK Banggol Peradong and SK Kampong Tengah in Terengganu, have already been completed ahead of schedule.
The remaining projects are expected to be completed in stages by December 2026, ahead of the 2027 Year One intake.
In a statement today, the ministry said the projects reflected the government's commitment to strengthening education infrastructure and ensuring a smooth transition for six-year-olds entering Year One.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kelantan police vow firm action against ‘tonto’ used to block enforcement in human‑smuggling cases
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Aug 19 — Police will take firm action against human-smuggling syndicates using ‘tonto’ to obstruct enforcement vehicles, following a recent incident in which two General Operations Force (GOF) personnel were hit while carrying out their duties.
Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the incident showed that the syndicates were becoming increasingly bold, stressing that such actions would not be tolerated.
“Human smuggling is a serious issue. They were willing to hit GOF personnel, which is an outrageous act that should not have happened,” he told a press conference at the Kelantan Police Contingent Headquarters (IPK) here today.
He said action would be taken against all parties involved under the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM), as well as Sections 353 and 186 of the Penal Code.
Mohd Yusoff said police had also detected human-smuggling activities using sea routes and rivers along the Kelantan coast, adding that enforcement agencies would remain vigilant against such operations.
He said the incident involving the GOF personnel was still considered an isolated case, but urged officers operating in the field, particularly GOF members and the Kelantan IPK task force, to remain alert and take appropriate action within the law when faced with threats.
On Aug 15, a land-based smuggler transporting six undocumented Myanmar women rammed two GOF personnel during an inspection at Kampung Chat Palekbang, Tumpat, before being arrested. — Bernama

Title: Immigration Dept opens internal probe after fatal KL crash that killed three
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Immigration Department today confirmed that one of its vehicles was involved in a fatal road accident along Jalan Sultan Ismail here early this morning.
In a statement posted on Facebook, Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department would give its full cooperation to the police in determining the cause of the accident.
“The department respects the ongoing investigation process and will not make any conclusions that could pre-empt the findings of the authorities,” he said.
Zakaria said the department would also conduct an internal investigation into compliance with standard operating procedures and safety aspects involving the operation of department vehicles to ensure the matter was thoroughly examined.
He urged those with information about the incident to assist the authorities, while asking the public to respect the privacy and sensitivities of the victims’ families and refrain from sharing unverified images, recordings or information.
Zakaria said the department viewed the incident seriously and would take appropriate action based on the findings of the police investigation and its internal probe.
The department also expressed its condolences and sympathy to the victims’ families and wished those receiving treatment a speedy recovery.

Title: MB: Pahang reports end of recorded hardcore poverty, with 2,913 households lifted and overall poverty down 30pc
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 19 — Pahang’s hardcore poverty was brought to an end on Feb 19, with all 2,913 heads of household recorded in the Jan 15, 2026 figure removed from the status, said Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail.
He said the state had also recorded a 30 per cent reduction in poverty, with 4,263 of the 14,210 heads of household classified as poor on June 5 subsequently removed from the category.
“The classification is based on the 2024 Poverty Line published by the Department of Statistics Malaysia under the Ministry of Economy,” he said in a statement today.
Wan Rosdy said key factors behind the achievement included targeted assistance, initiatives and interventions provided by the state and federal governments and relevant agencies, as well as changes in household income and household size.
According to him, households with a monthly per capita income below RM372 in urban areas and RM345 in rural areas are classified as hardcore poor, while those earning less than RM790 and RM714 respectively are classified as poor.
Wan Rosdy said a family’s status could also change due to changes in income, job losses and changes in household size, including children moving out to get married or take up employment.
“This milestone does not mean our efforts to eradicate poverty have come to an end. On the contrary, it requires continued action, monitoring and intervention, with the state government continuing to strengthen its poverty reduction efforts to ensure the benefits of prosperity and wellbeing reach people throughout Pahang,” he said.
He said the state government would continue to collaborate with the federal government, aid agencies, local authorities, elected representatives, and community leaders to ensure that families classified as poor or hardcore poor in the eKasih household poverty database receive the assistance they need.
“Our goal is not just to lift people out of poverty, but to help them become self-reliant, secure more stable incomes and achieve a better quality of life,” he said. — Bernama

Title: More workplace subsidies, tax incentives needed to support breastfeeding mothers, says Yeo Bee Yin
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — The government should provide more subsidies and tax incentives to companies to set up breastfeeding rooms and childcare facilities in the workplace.
Parliamentary Special Select Committee on Women, Children and Community Development chairman Yeo Bee Yin said such a move is necessary as many mothers find it challenging to continue breastfeeding after returning to work.
“In terms of the budget, as a Member of Parliament (for Puchong), I want more tax incentives for offices and companies to provide breastfeeding facilities.
“This includes breastfeeding rooms or multipurpose rooms where mothers can pump their milk, as well as childcare facilities in the workplace,” she said during a panel discussion titled ‘Realities of Breastfeeding’, held in conjunction with Toshiba Lifestyle Malaysia’s ‘World Breastfeeding Month 2026: Empowering Every Mother’s Journey’ event here yesterday.
Yeo launched the event, while the panel discussion, moderated by Nani Roslan, featured certified lactation consultant and infant care expert Elizabeth Richard and actress Natasha Hudson.
Yeo said breastfeeding and childcare issues often lacked sufficient attention in Parliament as women only made up about 13.5 per cent of the 222 Members of Parliament in Malaysia.
She emphasised that breastfeeding mothers required support from their families, employers and society, adding that they should not feel guilty when facing challenges such as low milk supply or breast engorgement.
“What children need most is a happy mother because that’s how they will grow up feeling safe and at peace. If you do not have enough milk or face difficulties, take it easy, seek treatment and take care of yourself,” she said.
Meanwhile, Elizabeth said mothers should refrain from self-blame when encountering breastfeeding difficulties as every baby is different, adding that those who cannot breastfeed directly could express and store their milk for their infants.
“Every child is different. A mother also learns new things with each child because their behaviour and her milk supply can be different. If you cannot breastfeed, it does not mean that you are a failure. You have tried, and there are other ways,” she said.
She added that those who are unable to breastfeed directly could express and store their milk for their infants, and that employers should be understanding of the time required for this process.
Actress and mother of five Natasha Hudson, 44, said she is still learning as every breastfeeding experience is different, noting that she had to combine breastfeeding with formula milk for the first time when her milk supply dropped while nursing her fourth daughter.
“I am always learning something new with every newborn. Even if I have experience, it does not mean that it will be the same because every child is different,” she said.
Natasha added that she received help from a lactation consultant while breastfeeding her fourth child and learned how to deal with mastitis, an inflammation of breast tissue that causes pain, swelling and redness. — Bernama

Title: Investment firm director previously charged with CBT now faces RM13.4m money‑laundering counts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — An investment company director, previously charged with criminal breach of trust, was brought before the Sessions Court here again today to face 10 charges of receiving RM13.4 million in proceeds from unlawful activities.
Datuk Norliza Tajudin, 54, pleaded not guilty after all the charges were read out individually before Judge Suzana Hussin.
She is charged with receiving the money through cheques and online transfers from a bank account belonging to Energy Eco Bhd.
The funds were allegedly transferred to her personal bank account and an account belonging to Aura Emas Trading Sdn Bhd, a company of which she is a director.
The offences were allegedly committed at three bank branches in Taman Setiawangsa, Wangsa Melawati and Bangsar here between Feb 1, 2021 and Feb 2, 2024.
All the charges were brought under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613), which is punishable under Section 4(1) of the same law.
The section provides a maximum prison sentence of 15 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the proceeds from the unlawful activities, or RM5 million, whichever is higher upon conviction.
Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurul Qistini Qamarul Abrar requested that the court apply the existing RM100,000 bail and the additional conditions set in the accused’s previous criminal breach of trust case.
“The prosecution also applies for this case to be tried jointly with the previous case (criminal breach of trust) in this court,” she said.
Lawyer Datuk Gobinath Mohanna, representing Norliza, did not object to the prosecution’s application.
Suzana Hussin subsequently granted the prosecution’s application on bail and for the two cases to be tried jointly. She also set Oct 29 for mention.
