On May 11, Norliza and the former Chairman of the Syariah Advisory Council (SAC) of Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), Tan Sri Dr Mohd Daud Bakar, pleaded not guilty in the same court to seven charges of criminal breach of trust involving RM10.55 million.
In the proceedings, the court granted bail of RM100,000 in one surety each to Norliza and Mohd Daud. They are also ordered to surrender their passports to the court, prohibited from interfering with prosecution witnesses, and to report to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office once a month. — Bernama

Title: Nilai private university CFO accused of RM6.56m CBT linked to IRB duty payments
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 19 — A chief financial officer (CFO) of a private university in Nilai pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to allegedly committing criminal breach of trust involving RM6.56 million in company funds between September 2025 and April this year.
Noraini Aripin, 55, entered the plea after the charge was read out to her before Judge Datin M. Kunasundary Marimuthu.
The charge alleges that Noraini, who was entrusted with RM6,557,720, misused the funds by making payments for purposes other than the payment of ad valorem duty to the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN).
The offence is alleged to have taken place at the university’s office between September 2025 and April this year.
She was charged under Section 409 of the Penal Code (Act 574), which carries a maximum sentence of 20 years’ imprisonment, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Syairah Aqilah Khalil sought bail of RM100,000 with two sureties, with the accused also required to surrender her passport to the court and report to the Negeri Sembilan Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office each month.
However, lawyer Kelvin Ong requested that bail be reduced to RM50,000, citing his client’s status as a mother of five, her ongoing treatment for stage-three breast cancer at a private hospital and her monthly income of RM15,000.
Bail was later set at RM80,000 with two sureties, with the judge also granting all the prosecution’s requests.
The court set September 21 for the next mention of the case. — Bernama

Title: Former UBB Investment Bank CEO pleads not guilty to RM139.8m cheating charge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — A former chief executive officer (CEO) of an investment bank pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of cheating regarding a payment of RM139.8 million to a private university management company.
Razlan Raghazli, 43, the former CEO of UBB Investment Bank Limited, entered the plea after the charge was read out to him before Judge Azura Alwi.
He was charged with cheating the Managing Director and CEO of UBB Amanah Berhad, Aida Aizura Othman, 52, by deceiving her into believing that the payment schedule contained in a UBB Investment Bank Limited letter was in accordance with legal advice.
The letter, titled ‘Disbursement Advice on Islamic Property Financing Under Bai-Bithaman Ajil (BBA)’ dated September 18, 2025, was signed by the accused and stated that it followed legal advice from the firm Kassim Tadin, Wai & Co.
However, the accused allegedly knew that the payment schedule in question actually contradicted the advice provided by the law firm.
The act allegedly caused Aida Aizura to release a payment amounting to RM139,891,776 to ELMU Higher Education Sdn Bhd, a payment she would not have made had she not been deceived in such a manner.
The offence, under Section 420 of the Penal Code, was allegedly committed at the bank in Desa Sri Hartamas in September 2025.
He faces imprisonment of up to 10 years, whipping, and is liable to a fine upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Hazel Tan Jia Qi proposed bail of RM100,000 with one surety, along with additional conditions requiring the accused to surrender his passport to the court and prohibiting him from interfering with or communicating with prosecution witnesses in the case.
However, lawyer Azamuddin Abdul Aziz, representing Razlan, requested that the bail amount be reduced to RM50,000, citing that his client had been unemployed since last June and had to support four children as well as an ailing mother.
Azura then set bail at RM60,000 with the additional conditions requested by the prosecution. She also set October 12 for mention and the submission of documents.
Meanwhile, the proceedings drew attention when lawyer Johan Mohan Abdullah, who is holding a watching brief for UBB, requested a court order prohibiting the media from naming the financial institution in their reports.
He argued that reports naming the institution could potentially undermine financial stability and trigger panic among depositors. However, Azura maintained that the public has a right to know further details regarding the case. — Bernama

Title: Police: Chinese national detained after allegedly disrupting passengers at KLIA, later admitted to psychiatric ward
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — A 27-year-old Chinese national who allegedly behaved aggressively towards passengers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport’s Terminal 1 building is believed to be mentally unwell and has been detained for further investigation, police said today.
KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M Ravi said authorities were alerted to the incident involving the woman at about 1.19pm on August 18, after she allegedly began shouting and disturbing passengers in the terminal's departure hall by running, singing and dancing.
"Security personnel later arrived at the scene and managed to calm the situation before bringing the woman to the Terminal 1 police station for further action.
"Her partner later told police that she had forgotten to take her prescribed medication," he said.
The woman was later taken to Hospital Kajang, where she was admitted to the psychiatric ward for further treatment.
He said the woman was scheduled to take a return flight to China that same day, having arrived in Malaysia with her partner as tourists on August 6.
Ravi said the woman was in stable condition and receiving treatment, while embassy officials had been informed of the incident.

Title: Kelana Jaya LRT services back to normal after Putra Heights safety system fault
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Rapid KL said the Kelana Jaya LRT Line resumed normal operations at 9.19am today after inspection and recovery works at Putra Heights station were completed.
The public transport operator said the earlier disruption was caused by a fault involving the station’s safety detection system.
“Checks and recovery measures have been carried out to ensure the system is operating safely,” it said.
Rapid KL said its technical team would continue monitoring the system and train movements to ensure services along the Kelana Jaya Line run smoothly.
It added that all trains have returned to their usual schedules and services affected by the disruption have fully recovered.
Earlier, Rapid KL said services were experiencing delays due to a suspected fault involving a power supply component at Putra Heights station, with trains there operated manually as a safety precaution.
Rapid KL apologised to passengers for the inconvenience caused by the train delays.

Title: Delays on Kelana Jaya LRT Line after suspected power supply fault
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Rapid KL said today that services on the Kelana Jaya LRT Line are experiencing delays due to a suspected fault involving a power supply component at Putra Heights station.
In a statement posted on Facebook, the public transport operator said trains at Putra Heights are being operated manually as a safety precaution.
It said this would also slow train movements at nearby stations and result in longer waiting times for passengers on platforms.
Rapid KL said its technical team has been deployed to the station to carry out checks and restore normal operations as soon as possible.
Auxiliary police and station personnel have also been stationed at concourse and platform areas to assist passengers, while regular announcements on train schedules are being made at stations.
Passengers were advised to check Rapid KL’s social media channels or the MyRapid PULSE journey-planning app for the latest updates on Kelana Jaya Line services.

Title: Saifuddin Nasution hits out at recycled false claims of Home Ministry granting citizenship en masse to foreigners
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has denied claims that the Home Ministry (KDN) granted citizenship en masse to foreign nationals and that 1.2 million Chinese nationals had remained in Malaysia.
Saifuddin Nasution said he had denied the allegations on numerous occasions, but some people continued to deliberately recycle videos, posters and narratives relating to the issue.
“I have repeatedly rejected these claims and have provided explanations backed by facts and official data.
“Yet some parties continue to deliberately recycle videos, posters and narratives that have already been corrected to confuse the public and stir racial tensions and hatred,” he said in a post on his official social media accounts today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the matter had already been explained officially, with the facts documented in earlier statements and media reports.
“The dissemination of such defamatory claims not only tarnishes the reputation of individuals or institutions, but more worryingly, can undermine public confidence in state institutions, stir racial hatred, disrupt public order and threaten national security,” he said.
He urged everyone to stop spreading such claims and not to exploit sensitive issues for political interests or social media attention.
“I also call on the public to check the accuracy of information with official sources before accepting or sharing it.
“Use social media responsibly. Facts are facts, and data is data. Do not let false claims override the truth,” he said.
Several posters alleging that KDN had granted citizenship to foreigners en masse have been widely circulated on social media. — Bernama

Title: ‘There may still be another way’: Sanusi signals Kedah will explore legal room to maintain zero-gambling stance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Kedah government will examine whether it has any legal avenues left to pursue its zero-gambling policy after the Federal Court rejected its bid to appeal a ruling over gambling licences, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has said.
Sanusi said the state had yet to decide on its next move and would first seek legal advice to ensure any further action complied with the court’s decision and did not risk contempt proceedings, according to
Utusan Malaysia
.
“How can anyone refuse to comply with a court order? That could amount to contempt of court. We cannot do that. I cannot provide an explanation because I do not have expertise in the matter,” he was quoted as saying.
“The lawyers will explain what the implications are, what is binding on us, and what we can and cannot do. There may still be another way. God willing, there is a way.”
He was speaking after a groundbreaking ceremony for a new student residential college at Sultan Abdul Halim Mu’adzam Shah International Islamic University (UniSHAMS) in Baling yesterday.
Asked whether the state government would issue new licences for gambling premises, Sanusi said no decision had been made.
“If no one wants to gamble, there is no need to open them. If there is no demand, naturally there will be no supply. I have not made that decision [on new licences]. We will see what the demand is like,” he said.
“My heart is with God. God does not permit it, but people do, so my heart remains with God.”
Sanusi also rejected suggestions that Kedah’s policy was intended to deny the rights of non-Muslims, saying the state government’s position was based on religious principles rather than ethnicity.
“I am still thinking about it when they say we are denying the rights of non-Muslims. We are not denying anyone’s rights. But if something is sinful, God commands us to prevent it,” he said.
“The problem is that Muslims can also enter [gambling premises]. That is the issue. As for the Chinese, since their religion does not prohibit gambling, go ahead and gamble. It is up to you. My heart is with God.”
Asked whether Kedah would use any remaining legal avenues to maintain its zero-gambling policy, Sanusi said the government first needed to establish what it could say or do following the judgment.
“I cannot say anything more yet. We have to see whether expressing such an intention could be regarded as contempt of court,” he said.
“But I can say that my heart is with God. Whoever accepts what is sinful is committing sin. That is the Islamic principle. To accept disbelief is disbelief.”
On August 12, the Federal Court dismissed the Kedah government’s application for leave to appeal against a Court of Appeal ruling concerning the issuance of licences for gambling premises.
The Court of Appeal had upheld an Alor Setar High Court decision finding that the Kedah government’s directive was
ultra vires
, or beyond its legal powers, and inconsistent with the Federal Constitution.

Title: Housing Ministry to nominate award-winning cleaning workers for state honours
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) plans to nominate recipients of the 2026 Cleaning Workers Award for state honours in recognition of their service and sacrifices in keeping public spaces clean.
Its Minister Nga Kor Ming said the proposal was discussed with KPKT secretary-general Datuk Dr Wira M Noor Azman Taib to ensure this year’s award recipients received due recognition for their contributions.
“I have discussed this with Datuk Wira, and this year’s national cleaning workers award recipients will be listed and nominated to the respective state palaces to receive honours from the respective state rulers,” he said in his speech at the 2026 Cleaning Workers Appreciation Day here yesterday.
Also present was Deputy Housing and Local Government Minister Datuk Aiman Athirah Sabu.
Nga said the practice of honouring the country’s cleaning workers had already been carried out by the Penang state government for almost 10 years.
“In my view, the time has come for our cleaning heroes in other states to also receive due recognition and appreciation,” he said.
He said the country’s solid waste management and public cleaning sector was currently supported by 26,889 workers employed by concessionaires.
“Many of them have served for more than a decade, while some have dedicated almost three decades, or 30 years, to the cleaning sector,” he said.
Nga said cleaning workers played an important role in keeping the country’s environment clean, safe and comfortable for the people, despite often working behind the scenes.
He also stressed that maintaining public cleanliness was not solely the responsibility of cleaning workers, but a shared responsibility among all Malaysians.
He said the habit of not littering must be instilled across all levels of society to realise the ‘Malaysia Bersih, Rakyat Sejahtera’ (Clean and Prosperous Malaysia) aspiration.
In this regard, he called on the Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation (SWCorp) to step up enforcement of the Community Service Order (PKM) to encourage greater public responsibility for maintaining cleanliness.
“As of Monday, August 17, a total of 14,807 offence notices had been issued this year. A total of 548 individuals have undergone Community Service Orders in states that have adopted Act 672.
“Of these, 419 have completed their Community Service Orders, while 129 are still serving them,” he said.
Nga stressed that the Community Service Order was not merely a form of punishment, but also an educational instrument to instil discipline, responsibility and awareness of public cleanliness.
At the event, seven workers received the 2026 Cleaning Workers Award, with two from Alam Flora Sdn Bhd and five from SWM Environment Sdn Bhd.
Contributions were also presented to three recipients as a gesture of support and concern for the welfare of cleaning workers. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar orders immediate Immigration probe into fatal Maju Junction crash, vows no compromise if wrongdoing found
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered the Immigration Department to immediately conduct a thorough investigation into a crash involving one of its trucks that killed three members of a family at Maju Junction here early today.
“If there was negligence or a breach of the law, appropriate action must be taken without compromise,” Anwar said in a Facebook post.
Anwar also extended his condolences over the of the tragedy.
According to preliminary police investigations, the crash occurred at about 1am when an Immigration Department Isuzu “Black Maria” truck entered the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection against a red light with its beacon lights and siren activated.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the truck collided with a Proton Saga travelling through a green light before skidding into four pedestrians from the same family and an Inokom Matrix.
A 53-year-old man and his two daughters, aged 25 and 12, died at the scene, while his 55-year-old wife was injured and taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital.
Police have detained the Immigration truck driver and the Proton Saga driver to assist investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.

Title: Crash with Immigration Dept truck at KL’s Maju Junction kills three family members
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Three members of a family were killed while another was injured after being hit by a Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) truck at the Maju Junction traffic light intersection on Jalan Sultan Ismail here early today.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the accident occurred at about 1am when the unladen Isuzu ‘Black Maria’ truck was travelling from the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Office towards Chow Kit for an operation targeting illegal immigrants.
He said preliminary investigations found that the truck, driven by a 43-year-old local man, entered the intersection against a red light with its beacon lights and siren activated.
“At the same time, a Proton Saga driven by a 50-year-old local man, which was travelling straight through a green light, was unable to avoid the truck and collided with it,” he said in a statement today.
Following the collision, the truck lost control and skidded before hitting four pedestrians, all members of the same family, as well as an Inokom Matrix driven by a 38-year-old local man.
Mohd Zamzuri said the three pedestrians who died at the scene were a 53-year-old man and his two daughters, aged 25 and 12.
His 55-year-old wife sustained injuries to her head, arm and both legs and is currently receiving treatment in the Red Zone at Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL).
The drivers of the JIM truck, Proton Saga and Inokom Matrix were uninjured.
“The driver of the JIM lorry and the driver of the Proton Saga have been detained to assist with the investigation. Breathalyser and preliminary urine screening tests found them negative for alcohol and drugs,” he said.
He added that police were conducting further investigations at the scene, including obtaining CCTV footage and identifying independent witnesses, to assist investigations under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Members of the public with information on the incident are urged to contact the Jalan Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Housing minister urges waste separation to be taught young as Malaysia studies Japan’s recycling model
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Malaysia is looking to Japan’s waste separation and recycling practices as it seeks to make environmentally responsible habits part of everyday life and accelerate the country’s transition towards a circular economy.
Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said Japan’s experience in efficient waste management, particularly its practice of separating waste at source, could provide valuable lessons for Malaysia.
“Japan is well known for its efficient waste management system and strong culture of cleanliness. In Japan, separating waste at source has become part of everyday life. This is something we can learn from.
“Good habits must start from young. We should teach our children about waste separation, recycling and keeping our surroundings clean, so that cleanliness becomes part of our culture and not something we do only because of enforcement,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Nga said Malaysia and Japan were set to strengthen cooperation in advancing the circular economy and modernising waste management through a proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the two countries.
The MoU, which he said was approved by the Cabinet last month, is expected to facilitate the exchange of expertise, technology and best practices between the two countries.
Nga discussed the proposed cooperation during a courtesy visit to Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Noriyuki Shikata at the ambassador’s official residence here yesterday.
He said Malaysia had already introduced several measures to support the transition, including the National Circular Economy Blueprint and the establishment of the National Circular Economy Council (NCEC), as well as requiring shopping malls to provide recycling facilities as part of licensing requirements and continuing efforts to phase out single-use plastic bags.
“By combining Japan’s experience and technological expertise with Malaysia’s ongoing reforms, we can accelerate our transition towards cleaner, greener and more sustainable cities,” Nga said.
Meanwhile, Shikata invited the Malaysian delegation to attend GREEN×EXPO 2027 in Yokohama, which could provide further opportunities for cooperation in areas including smart and sustainable cities. — Bernama

Title: ‘I only wanted to save’: Kajang retiree wins RM1m Bank Rakyat lucky draw
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — A 68-year-old retiree never thought that his decision to save through Bank Rakyat’s Rizq Plus Investment-i Account would bring him such good fortune when he emerged as the winner of the Millionaire Draw, taking home a RM1 million prize.
Aziz Mohamed, from Kajang, Selangor, said he joined Rizq Plus after being introduced to the product by a Bank Raykat officer, with the intention of saving his surplus funds.
“I only put the money in to save, I never intended to win anything,” he told Bernama after the
Raikan Ganjaran #UntukSemua
(#Untuk Semua Rewards Celebration) here yesterday.
On his plans for the prize money, Aziz said he would keep the money in the investment account, adding that he also plans to go on a holiday with his family.
Meanwhile, Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Mohd Irwan Mohd Mubarak said that Aziz is the fifth millionaire since the Rizq Plus Investment-i account was introduced in 2022.
“The next Millionaire Draw is in October,” he said in his speech at the ceremony.
The Rizq Plus Investment-i account currently has over 250,000 customers, with total investments exceeding RM1 billion.
At the same event, 40-year-old Awang Ahmad Khadar Awang Zainal, from Mukah, Sarawak, emerged as the winner of the Suara Hati 2026 Campaign, taking home the grand prize of a Toyota Fortuner sports utility vehicle (SUV).
The February 19-April 30 campaign also saw four winners each receiving gold wafers weighing 50 grammes, 30 grammes and 20 grammes, as well as home furnishings worth RM10,000, while 65 winners received consolation prizes of RM500 credited to their Rizq Plus Investment-i Account. — Bernama

Title: Govt must not to replace UUCA with another ‘oppressive’ law, says deputy education minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The new legal framework to be introduced following the repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA) 1971 must strengthen university autonomy and academic freedom and avoid repeating the shortcomings of the repealed Act, said Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abd Halim.
He said the new framework should bring reforms in various aspects, including ensuring more meaningful student participation in the governance of higher education institutions.
“We must really ensure that we can achieve the changes and reforms that we have been advocating all this while. In other words, the repeal of UUCA must not lead to its replacement with another law that is equally oppressive, as has been opposed all this while.
“It should create a platform or an opportunity for all universities and the higher education sector to become more progressive,” he said when contacted during the Reaksi segment produced by Bernama Radio yesterday.
He said the process of drafting the framework will involve broad and inclusive consultations with all stakeholders, including student representatives, university leadership, academics and policymakers.
Adam Adli said the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) has referred to various historical records, legal interpretations and fundamental recommendations such as the One Higher Education Act outlined in the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint to ensure that the new framework was built on clear principles.
“We must develop a new framework that is developmental and liberating, and can truly fulfil a university’s potential as a place for the advancement of knowledge, healthy debate, and the freedom to learn and pursue academic activities.
“We must ensure that all relevant parties are involved to ensure that there are no backdoor clauses and the like. We must create broader avenues and more meaningful consultations for all parties who will come under the protection of the Act to be introduced soon,” he said.
On Sunday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government gave its assurance that UUCA would be fully repealed without introducing any new laws that are restrictive or oppressive towards student movements.
Previously, UUCA had undergone seven rounds of amendments since it was introduced in 1971, including amendments in 2012 that allowed students to participate in political party activities outside campus.
The latest amendments in 2024 saw disciplinary action against students at public universities no longer come under the authority of the vice-chancellor, but instead be decided by the Student Disciplinary Committee through amendments to Section 16B of UUCA.
Dr Anuar Ahmad, Deputy Director of the Malaysian Inclusive Development and Advancement Institute (MINDA) at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, was previously reported as saying that the repeal of UUCA 1971 should be followed by the establishment of a high-level committee to examine the new legal framework that would ensure the governance and management of higher education institutions remained safeguarded. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia: Over 90pc chance of ‘Super El Nino’ by year-end, could rival 1997–1998 extreme
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — The likelihood of El Nino, which typically brings hotter and drier conditions, reaching the ‘very strong’ or ‘Super El Nino’ category between October and December has risen to more than 90 per cent, according to Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip.
He said the forecast was based on a significant upward trend in the Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) since the middle of the year, coupled with recent weekly observations showing sea surface temperatures more than 1.8 degrees Celsius above the climatological average.
“This situation indicates that El Nino is continuing to strengthen and is expected to peak towards the end of 2026.
“The probability of El Nino reaching the very strong category between October and December 2026 is high, at more than 90 per cent, based on the latest forecasts issued by international climate models,” he told Bernama.
Mohd Hisham said current global climate patterns indicated that the 2026-2027 El Nino could rank among the most extreme events ever recorded, with its impact potentially exceeding or at least matching that of the very strong El Nino episodes in 1997-1998 and 2015-2016.
The highest temperature recorded during the 1997-1998 El Nino episode was 40.1 degrees Celsius at the Chuping Meteorological Station in Perlis on April 9, 1998, while the 2015-2016 episode saw 39.3 degrees Celsius recorded at the Batu Embun Meteorological Station in Jerantut, Pahang, on April 10, 2016.
“Experience during the Super El Nino episodes in those years showed that the country experienced hotter and drier conditions than usual, accompanied by a significant reduction in rainfall in some areas towards the end of the Northeast Monsoon (NEM) and during the inter-monsoon period between February and May.
“Based on the patterns of previous episodes and the effects of global warming in recent years, the increase in temperatures this time is expected to be more pronounced from February to May next year,” he said.
Mohd Hisham said the strong El Nino was also expected to occur alongside a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), potentially intensifying the reduction in rainfall across the region.
“El Nino reduces the supply of moisture from the Pacific Ocean, while a positive IOD reduces the supply of moisture from the Indian Ocean,” he said.
“The combination increases the likelihood of hotter and drier conditions, as well as longer spells without rain, across the southern Asean region, including Malaysia,” he said.
Mohd Hisham assured that MetMalaysia would continue to closely monitor developments involving both phenomena, as well as weather conditions and the regional risk of forest fires.
He said that during a positive IOD phase, sea surface temperatures in the eastern Indian Ocean near Indonesia were relatively cooler than those in the western Indian Ocean.
“This typically reduces cloud formation and rainfall over Indonesia and parts of Southeast Asia,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest man suspected of setting 62-year-old Kepong lottery shop worker on fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Police have arrested a suspect in connection with the Aug 9 attack on an elderly woman who was doused with petrol and set alight at a lottery outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong.
Sentul Police acting chief Supt Jasni Zolpa confirmed the arrest when contacted.
“Yes, the suspect has been arrested and a press conference will be held today,” he said.
The elderly woman suffered burns to about 50 per cent of her body after she was doused with a liquid believed to be petrol and set alight at the premises.
Jasni said police were alerted at about 8am that the 62-year-old victim, who worked at the counter, had been attacked by an unidentified man. — Bernama

Title: Former investment bank CEO among three to face MACC charges involving over RM136m
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Three individuals, including a former chief executive officer (CEO) of an investment bank, are expected to be charged under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act at the Sessions Courts in Kuala Lumpur and Seremban today.
According to the court system, the former CEO will be charged before Sessions Court Judge Azura Alwi while a woman with the title Datuk, who is a company director, will be charged before Sessions Court Judge Suzana Hussin.
The former CEO is understood to face charges involving more than RM130 million in alleged corruption, while the woman had previously been linked to an investment investigated by MACC and had also been charged in court with criminal breach of trust.
The third individual, a chief financial officer (CFO) of a private higher education institution, is expected to face charges involving RM6.56 million in alleged corruption before Sessions Court Judge Kunasundary Marimuthu at the Seremban Sessions Court. — Bernama

Article:

reported that the couple, who became engaged on March 28, revealed their wedding date during entertainment programme
MeleTOP

Title: UUCA explained: Malaysia’s 55-year-old campus control law and the repeal now on the table
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) is set to be repealed, marking the end of a contentious 55-year legal era that defined, and often stifled, student activism in Malaysia.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim made the landmark announcement during the PKR Congress on Saturday, promising that no new legislation intended to curtail freedom of expression would replace the outgoing Act.
Since its inception in April 1971, UUCA has undergone seven amendments. However, none of these incremental changes managed to silence the decades-long demand for its total abolition.
The road to restriction
The UUCA was Malaysia’s answer to a wave of student unrest in the early-to-mid 1970s, when university students were among the country’s most vocal critics of poverty and inequality.
The turning point came in 1974, when students organised mass demonstrations in solidarity with impoverished rubber tappers and peasant farmers, culminating in the Baling protests that November — thousands-strong rallies that put pressure on the government and landed student leaders, including a young Anwar Ibrahim, in detention.
At the time, Anwar was president of Abim (Angkatan Belia Islam Malaysia, or the Malaysian Islamic Youth Movement), which he co-founded in 1971.
The UUCA was tightened to curtail student activism following the Baling incident in December 1974.
Students protest against the arrest of activists in Kuala Lumpur on February 2, 2025. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Originally introduced to replace an emergency ordinance, the 1975 amendment, pushed by then-education minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, was designed to rein in a surging tide of student activism. These changes introduced secret ballots for student elections and, more significantly, Sections 15 and 16, which allowed for the summary suspension or expulsion of students.
The amendment also granted the education minister sweeping powers, including the authority to advise the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the appointment of vice-chancellors and the direct appointment of university council members. Positions like deans and heads of institutes, previously determined by internal elections, became direct appointments by the vice-chancellor.
In 1996, a further amendment centralised this power. The minister gained the right to appoint all eight members of a university’s Board of Directors. The university senate, once a robust body of all deans and professors, was downsized to a smaller group of institutional leaders and a handful of professors handpicked by the vice-chancellor.
Students march during an anti-racism rally organized by the Universiti Malaya student union at Universiti Malaya in Kuala Lumpur on September 5, 2019. — Picture by Yusof Mat Isa
A decade of “relaxation” was not enough
Successive governments began relaxing these constraints starting in 2009. Criminal penalties were removed, and a 2012 amendment allowed students to join political parties outside of campus following a landmark Court of Appeal ruling.
By 2018, students were permitted to participate in political activities within their own campuses.
The most recent update in 2024 saw student disciplinary committees take over the power to punish students from the vice-chancellor, while student bodies gained greater financial autonomy.
Despite these concessions, critics argued the “spirit” of the Act remained punitive. Vice-chancellors still held broad powers to dissolve student groups or punish those deemed to be acting against the university’s interests.
A recent flashpoint occurred in June 2025, when 13 students at Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) faced potential suspension or expulsion for participating in an anti-corruption rally in Kota Kinabalu.
While Anwar eventually intervened to urge the university against such harsh measures, the incident highlighted the fact that as long as UUCA existed, student freedom remained subject to the whims of the administration.
Posters are seen at Universiti Malaya ahead of campus elections in Kuala Lumpur on June 17, 2022. — Picture by Choo Choy May
Student groups want clear timeline
While student leaders have welcomed the announcement, the mood remains one of cautious optimism. Groups are now pushing for concrete legislative action rather than verbal promises.
Himpunan Advokasi Rakyat Malaysia (Haram), a coalition of five student groups from the Peninsula and Sabah, has called on the government to table the motion for repeal during the next Dewan Rakyat sitting.
The group is also advocating for the creation of an independent tribunal to hear student disciplinary appeals, as well as greater transparency in how vice-chancellors are appointed.
Similarly, the Universiti Malaya Association of New Youth (Umany) has urged the government to provide a specific timeline for the repeal.
The group also called on all higher learning institutions to immediately cease all ongoing probes and disciplinary actions against students initiated under the Act.

Title: Sarawak eyes direct Kuching–Jeju flights as AirBorneo expands regional tourism links
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 18 — Sarawak is seeking to establish direct AirBorneo Airways (AirBorneo) connectivity between Kuching and Jeju Island in South Korea as the state moves to expand access to key regional tourism markets.
Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said South Korea was among the markets being considered for AirBorneo, with Jeju Island identified for the proposed direct connection.
“Korea is one of the destinations that we are going to have AirBorneo flying to. We hope to have that connectivity between Kuching and Jeju Island, not Incheon.
“Jeju is recognised as a World Natural Heritage and Global Geopark under Unesco, and Kuching is on the way to being recognised as a Unesco Global Geopark.
“As previously mentioned by the Premier, he wants to establish a direct flight between Jeju Island and Kuching, most probably after Jakarta,” he told a press conference after the opening of the Pacific Asia Travel Association (PATA) Travel Mart (PTM) here on Tuesday.
Abdul Karim said Jakarta was expected to be the next AirBorneo destination in September, followed by either Bangkok or Jeju Island.
Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said South Korea was among the markets being considered for AirBorneo, with Jeju Island identified for the proposed direct connection. — The Borneo Post pic
On Dec 6 last year, Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg expressed interest in establishing direct services to Jeju Island, saying the connection could link Jeju’s geopark with Sarawak’s own geopark.
Describing South Korea as a promising market for Sarawak, Abdul Karim said there was strong interest among Sarawakians in travelling there, while the state also had opportunities to attract more Korean visitors.
“I personally see that Korea is a very, very good market. We are very, very impressed with how Koreans live their lives.
“Whatever things that they touch, they turn it to gold,” he said.
He said Sarawak could also learn from South Korea’s development, particularly its efforts to nurture younger generations and build globally recognised industries in music, technology, automobiles and sports.
Abdul Karim also highlighted the growing interest among Korean families in sending their children to Kuching to study English at international schools, saying this reflected confidence in the city as an education destination.
His remarks on expanding regional air connectivity come as Sarawak continues to face limitations in direct international access.
Also speaking at the press conference, PATA chief executive officer Noor Ahmad Hamid said this was among the challenges faced in bringing international travellers to the state.
“We took a risk when we decided to bring PATA Travel Mart to Sarawak because Sarawak is not a destination that has many direct flights compared with Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok or Singapore,” he said.
Despite this, Noor Ahmad said PTM 2026 attracted more than 1,100 delegates from 48 countries, including over 220 buyers representing about 215 companies from 29 source markets.
He said PATA also saw strong potential in Asean, which remained relatively untapped despite its proximity to Sarawak.
“China and India are certainly big markets, but Asean is also a huge untapped market, and it is right next door to Sarawak,” he said.
PATA Travel Mart is a major Asia-Pacific tourism trade event bringing together buyers, sellers and industry players, with PATA using the platform to support its members and promote destinations across the region.
Also present were Sarawak Tourism Board chief executive officer Sharzede Datu Salleh Askor, PATA chairman Henry Oh and Ministry of Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts permanent secretary Morshidi Fredrick. — The Borneo Post

Title: Kuala Pilah school lab roof collapse prompts chemical removal, JKR to assess safety
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Aug 18 — The roof of a laboratory at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Juasseh here suddenly collapsed at noon today.
Kuala Pilah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Commander, Senior Fire Officer Mohd Idham Mohd Rodzi said no casualties were reported in the incident.
He said firefighters rushed to the scene after receiving an emergency call and found that part of the roof of the three-storey school building had collapsed.
“Further inspection found that no one was involved in the incident as the room was empty at the time.
“Several chemicals in the room were removed and relocated to a safer place as we were concerned that they could potentially cause a fire,” he told Bernama here today.
Mohd Idham said the area had been cordoned off and was to remain off-limits until it was deemed completely safe.
He said the case was subsequently referred to the Public Works Department (JKR) for further assessment. — Bernama

Title: 1MDB civil trial: Shahrol Azral denies Jho Low acted as PM, insists Najib briefed indirectly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Former 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi told the High Court today that he did not “treat” fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, or Jho Low, as the country’s Prime Minister.
However, the 56-year-old, testifying as the fourth plaintiff witness in 1MDB’s US$5.64 billion civil suit, said he had communicated with then prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak through informal channels, namely via Jho Low.
He said this during cross-examination by lawyer G.K. Ganesan, who represents former 1MDB investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jin, the seventh defendant in the suit.
The issue arose when Ganesan asked whether Shahrol Azral had communicated directly with Najib about the dispute between two countries over the Serdar oil field project, which was related to the RM1 billion joint venture deal.
Ganesan: Did you think it was important or enough for the sitting prime minister (Najib) to know that two different countries were fighting over ownership of the Serdar oil field?
Shahrol Azral: Yes.
The witness also admitted that he did not know whether Jho Low had informed Najib about the dispute involving the Serdar oil field project.
Ganesan: For all intents and purposes, you treated Jho Low as if he was the prime minister of Malaysia.
Shahrol Azral: I disagree
1MDB and its subsidiaries — 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited, 1MDB Energy Limited, 1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited and Global Diversified Investment Company Limited, formerly known as 1MDB Global Investments Limited - filed the civil suit on May 7, 2021.
They named former prime minister Najib, 1MDB’s former finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng, former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee, former general counsel Jasmine Loo Ai Swan, Vincent Beng, former chief financial officer Radhi Mohamad, Kelvin Tan, and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.
Last week, 1MDB dropped its civil suit against Radhi, with no liberty to refile. The company had previously removed Jasmine from the case as well.
The writ of summons stated that the plaintiffs, among other things, accused the defendants of breach of trust, breach of statutory duty, abuse of power and conspiracy to misappropriate 1MDB funds.
The trial before Judicial Commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus resumes tomorrow. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain, strong winds forecast in multiple states, MetMalaysia issues evening alert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across several areas in Peninsular Malaysia until 9pm today.
In a statement, it said the affected areas include the whole of Perlis and several districts in Kedah, namely Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Pokok Sena, Padang Terap, Yan and Pendang.
A similar warning has also been issued for several areas in Perak (Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang and Kerian); Kelantan (Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Mas, Kota Bharu and Tumpat); Pahang (Maran, Rompin, Pekan and Kuantan); and Johor (Johor Bahru). — Bernama

Title: Court adjourns Pulau Batu Puteh appeal, Dr Mahathir’s lawyer seeks to add RCI report
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — The Court of Appeal here today adjourned the hearing of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad’s appeal after his lawyer indicated that he would file an application to adduce the Pulau Batu Puteh Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report as fresh evidence in the appeal.
The three-member bench comprising Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan, Datuk Ong Chee Kwan and Datuk Seri Mohd Radzi Harun allowed Dr Mahathir’s lawyer, Zainur Zakaria, two weeks to file the application.
The court also fixed Sept 10 for case management to set a date for continuation of the appeal hearing.
During the proceedings, Zainur argued that the findings of the RCI had implicated Dr Mahathir as being the person responsible for the loss of the Pulau Batu Puteh and had also recommended that prosecution be initiated against his client.
He said when the High Court judge decided on his client’s judicial review application, the RCI report was not available.
However, senior federal counsel Shamsul Bolhassan, representing eight respondents, including RCI Chairman Tun Md Raus Sharif, said the court could not take judicial notice of the report or allow Dr Mahathir’s lawyer to introduce the report as fresh evidence.
He said the findings of the RCI had already been presented and submitted to the Yang-di-Pertuan Agong.
Dr Mahathir is appealing against the High Court’s decision on Jan 13, 2025, which dismissed his judicial review application seeking a mandamus order to compel the RCI to allow him and his counsel to attend the RCI proceedings.
In the judicial review application filed in 2024, Dr Mahathir claimed that he had requested to attend the entire duration of the RCI proceedings with his counsel pursuant to Section 18 of the Commission of Enquiry Act 1950, but his request was rejected.
On May 23, 2008, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) ruled that Singapore has sovereignty over Batu Puteh, while Middle Rocks, less than a kilometre from the island, belonged to Malaysia. The ownership of South Ledge, about four kilometres from Batu Puteh, would be determined based on the maritime boundaries of the controlling country.
On Feb 14, 2024, the RCI was set up to inquire into Dr Mahathir’s decision to withdraw an application to review the ICJ’s decision. On June 12, 2024, Dr Mahathir testified in the RCI proceedings, which were conducted behind closed doors.
The Commissioners concluded the inquiry and handed their report to the Yang-di-Pertuan Agong on Aug 12, 2024. The RCI later declassified its report issued on Dec 5, 2024. — Bernama

Title: Sabah Fire Dept issues stern warning as eight areas hit by 12‑day dry spell
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 18 — Eight areas across seven districts in Sabah are experiencing a prolonged dry spell, with between 12 and 14 consecutive days without rain recorded as of yesterday.
Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Mohd Pisar Aziz said areas that had gone without rain for more than a week were categorised as being at high risk of fires and haze.
“Therefore, the Fire and Rescue Department is issuing a stern warning to the public against carrying out any open burning that could further worsen the current dry conditions,” he said in a statement today.
He said Keningau and Pitas recorded the longest dry spell, at 14 consecutive days, followed by the Wario Livestock Centre in Kota Belud and Ranau Station, at 13 days each.
He added that four other locations — the Kimanis Agriculture Office in Papar, Laban Rata at Mount Kinabalu in Ranau, Serinsim Sub-Station in Kota Marudu and Kota Kinabalu Station — had recorded 12 consecutive days without rainfall.
Mohd Pisar also stressed that those found carrying out open burning could face legal action or hefty fines under the Environmental Quality Act 1974 (Act 127). — Bernama

Title: High Court to deliver Aug 24 ruling on Negeri Sembilan Undang eviction summons
Article:
SEREMBAN, Aug 18 — The High Court today set Aug 24 for its decision on an originating summons filed by the Negeri Sembilan state government seeking an immediate eviction order for the official halls and residences of the Undang Rembau and Undang Sungei Ujong.
Judge Roz Mawar Rozain set the date after hearing submissions from the state government’s counsel Muhammad Hariz Md Yusoff, and lawyers Choo Shi Jin and Asmawi Ismail, representing Abdul Rahim Yasin and Datuk Mubarak Thahak, respectively.
“The court sets Aug 24 for the decision at 4pm via Zoom,” said the judge.
The Negeri Sembilan state government filed separate originating summonses against Abdul Rahim and Mubarak on 16 and 17 July, respectively.
Besides Abdul Rahim and Mubarak, other respondents named include occupants or individuals residing at the official halls and residences of Undang Rembau and Undang Sungei Ujong.
The state government, as the owner of the premises, is seeking an order affirming its right to vacant possession of all four premises, as well as a declaration that the respondents and any other occupants still residing there are trespassers without legal right, licence, or permission from the applicant.
The state government is also seeking an order for all respondents to immediately move and hand over vacant possession of the premises.
Earlier, Muhammad Hariz argued that the state government has locus standi (legal standing) to file the summons under Section 22(1) of the Government Proceedings Act, read together with Sections 5, 16(1)(c), and 40 of the National Land Code.
“The applicant is the Negeri Sembilan state government, the lawful owner and authority over the premises, which have been gazetted as public reserve land under Section 62 of the National Land Code,” he said.
He said eviction notices were served on April 29 and June 29, but the respondents are still occupying the premises.
Muhammad Hariz said Abdul Rahim occupies the official hall and residence of Undang Rembau based on prior permission or licence granted in his capacity as the Undang Luak Rembau.
He said an official notice from the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) dated Aug 1, 2026, had finalised the position regarding the rightful holder of the Undang Luak Rembau title.
“To date, the applicant has been unable to access the government premises for nearly 50 days,” he said.
He was assisted by Negeri Sembilan state legal advisor Ala’uddin Baharom and lawyer Ahmad Khalil Md Rofiee.
Meanwhile, Choo objected to the originating summons, arguing that the applicant was not the proper party to bring the action.
He pointed out that control and administration of state land vests in the state director of Lands and Mines, not the state government.
“Even in the applicant’s own case, no right of possession is vested in the applicant, as the said premises are unalienated state land with no registered proprietor at all.
“The care and maintenance of the said reserve, according to the applicant’s own gazette notifications, vests in the district officer of Rembau, and not the applicant,” he said.
Asmawi, adopting Choo’s arguments, also contended that the state government lacks locus standi to file the originating summons.
Previously, Mubarak was reported to have been stripped of his position as the Undang Luak Sungei Ujong. — Bernama
